checks.summary: Your bot protection lets in anyone who claims to be a known AI agent.

checks.fix: Stop allowlisting by User-Agent. Admit named agents only when their Web Bot Auth signature verifies (agent-doorman verifies signatures; many CDNs can too).

checks.title: Fake signatures buy nothing
checks.summary: No signature checking observed: a fake signature was treated like any other visit.
checks.fix: Verify Web Bot Auth signatures so you can tell real agents from impostors, and require verification on transactional paths.

checks.title: Transactional pages need proof
checks.summary: Unverified agent claims reach the extra pages you listed.
checks.fix: Require a browser or a verified agent on cart, checkout and account paths (see the ecommerce preset). The audit only sends GET requests, so this is a signal, not proof that actions are possible.

checks.title: Refusals explain themselves
checks.summary: Only 0/2 refusals told the agent why or how to get in.
checks.fix: Answer refused agents with a JSON body and an Accept-Signature header (Web Bot Auth §4.3) or Retry-After, not an HTML wall.

checks.title: Verified agents get in
checks.summary: Not tested. Pass --sign-key (and --signature-agent) to check that a signed agent is admitted.

checks.title: robots.txt states an agent policy
checks.fix: Publish robots.txt with explicit groups for the AI crawlers you allow or refuse.

checks.title: Pages are discoverable
checks.fix: Publish a sitemap and reference it from robots.txt.

checks.title: llms.txt summary
checks.fix: Optional: publish /llms.txt, a short Markdown guide to your site for language models (proposal at llmstxt.org).

checks.title: Published agent policy
checks.summary: No /.well-known/agent-policy.json (optional, experimental format served by agent-doorman).

checks.title: Language is declared
checks.fix: Set <html lang="..."> so agents pick the right language model behaviour and locale.

checks.title: Title and description
checks.summary: 2 page(s) miss a title or meta description.
checks.fix: Give every page a specific <title> and <meta name="description">.

checks.title: Structured data
checks.summary: No JSON-LD found on audited pages.
checks.fix: Add schema.org JSON-LD (Organization, Product with offers, BreadcrumbList...) so agents read facts instead of guessing from layout.

checks.title: Content without JavaScript
checks.summary: 2 page(s) show little or no text before JavaScript runs.
checks.fix: Server-render (or pre-render) key content. Agents that fetch HTML without running scripts see an empty shell.

categories.title: Can agents fill in your forms

checks.title: Every field has a label
checks.summary: 0/4 fields have a label or accessible name.
checks.fix: Use <label for>, a wrapping <label> or aria-label. Placeholders vanish when typing and many agents ignore them.

checks.title: Fields say what they are
checks.summary: 0/4 identity, contact, address and payment fields carry an autocomplete token.
checks.fix: Add autocomplete tokens (email, tel, given-name, street-address, postal-code, cc-number, current-password...). They tell agents and password managers exactly what each field wants.

checks.title: Buttons are named
checks.summary: 0/1 buttons have a text or accessible name.
checks.fix: Give icon-only buttons an aria-label that says what they do ("Add to cart", not "button").

checks.title: Inputs use specific types
checks.fix: Use type="email" and type="tel" so agents format and validate input correctly.

checks.title: Browser-like visits get through
checks.summary: Plain browser requests reached every audited page.

checks.title: No CAPTCHA in the way
checks.summary: Challenge technology found on audited pages: reCAPTCHA.
checks.fix: Keep challenges for suspicious traffic and let verified agents skip them; otherwise legitimate agents stall at this step.
